matchups.recap: Rob got absolutely skull-fucked this week, dropping 96.5 points like he was trying to tank for draft position—except his ass is already locked out of the playoffs. Ben put up 115.9 and didn't even break a sweat, while Rob's roster looked like a practice squad reject bin. That 19.4 point margin isn't just a loss, it's a full-on public execution, and Rob's gonna be hearing about this one until next season's draft.

Nori got absolutely cock-slapped by 23.7 points this week, and honestly that's generous considering how fucking lifeless that 93.6 looked on the scoreboard. You brought a wet noodle to a gunfight, and Veton didn't even have to try that hard to leave you in the dust. Time to check the waiver wire and find whatever garbage player you'll inevitably reach for this week while your season circles the drain.

Faton got absolutely robbed by 4.6 points—which is exactly how many brain cells he was using when he benched his flex and left points rotting on the bench like last week's grocery store sushi. 113.6 to 109.0 isn't just a loss, it's a masterclass in snatching defeat from the jaws of victory, and Arben's sitting here laughing all the way to the W column while Faton's out here wondering if his waiver wire has an undo button.

Ilir got absolutely pummeled 104.6 to 77.9—that's a 26.7 point ass-beating that'll echo through the league chat for weeks. Whatever dogshit lineup decisions you made this week, they didn't just lose you the game, they got embarrassed by nearly 27 points. Flamur walked out of there with his dick out while you're sitting there wondering how your roster managed to underperform this spectacularly.

Jetmir and Peter got absolutely cucked by 2.8 fucking points—that's the fantasy equivalent of showing up to a gunfight with a knife made of wet noodles. Two heads, one brain between them, and it still couldn't figure out how to not leave 15 points on the bench while watching Rinor coast to victory like he was playing against a JV squad. Better luck next week, boys—though honestly, with that combined roster management, you'll need it.

Rilind got absolutely fucking demolished this week, losing by nearly 24 points like he forgot half his roster was on bye week. Adam's team showed up ready to play while Rilind's lineup looked like he set it on his phone while taking a shit and never looked back. That's not a loss, that's a mercy killing—Adam just put Rilind's fantasy season out of its misery.

matchups.preview: Rob's clinging to life support at 2-5, but don't worry—Veton's here to pull the plug with a 1-6 dumpster fire that makes Rob's season look like a championship run. This is what happens when two teams decided the draft was more of a suggestion than a roadmap, and now they're both just praying their waiver wire pickups develop sentience. Whoever loses this one gets to spend the week convincing themselves they're still in it.

Faton's sitting pretty at 4-3, but let's not forget this is the same guy who's been limping through the season like his roster has a collective hamstring injury. Ben's desperate at 3-4 and will probably throw everything at the wall this week, but desperation doesn't win fantasy football—it just makes the loss hurt more. Faton should cruise, assuming he doesn't pull off some vintage mid-season collapse bullshit that we all know he's capable of.

Two mediocre fucks both clinging to .500 like it's a life raft—congrats on being exactly average, you absolute disasters. Ilir's been carried by waiver-wire desperation all season while Nori's roster is held together with duct tape and false hope, so expect both of you to completely implode in the most uninspiring fashion possible this week.

Jetmir and Peter limping in at 4-3 are about to get absolutely humbled by Arben's 6-1 juggernaut—turns out running a competent roster all season actually pays off, who knew? Y'all have been coasting on luck and waiver-wire desperation for seven weeks; Arben's about to remind everyone what real fantasy management looks like.

Rilind's bringing a dumpster fire to face the league's hottest team, and honestly, this matchup feels less like a game and more like a mercy killing—Flamur's about to add another body to the pile while Rilind's out here desperately hoping his waiver-wire desperation plays don't completely implode on national television again. At 1-6, you've had seven chances to prove you know what you're doing, and you've failed spectacularly every single time, so why would this week be any different?

Adam's sitting at 3-4 with what looks like a roster held together by duct tape and false hope, while Rinor's actually managed to sneak into respectability at 4-3—but we both know this is the week Adam's desperation finally pays off and he somehow pulls off the upset, because that's how this shit works when you've got nothing left to lose and everything to prove. Rinor's about to get blindsided by a guy who's been streaming defenses like he's looking for the meaning of life, and honestly, it might just work out this one time before he crashes back to earth next week.
